key_insight: A data-driven algorithm can automatically detect multiscale self-similarity in turbulent flows and recover both classical scaling laws and their corrections from simulation data.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, equation-agnostic tool for extracting inner, outer, and intermediate scaling behavior in turbulence models and measurements.
method: Extends prior single-scale self-similarity identification to multiscale settings
Applies the algorithm to channel flow and decaying turbulence data
Recovers similarity expressions and associated scaling laws from each flow region
evidence_signal: In numerical data for turbulent channel flow and both late- and early-stage homogeneous decaying turbulence, the method identifies inner/outer similarity and reveals intermediate-region laws such as the log law and -5/3 spectrum.
watch_item: The inferred similarity forms depend on having sufficiently resolved multiscale data, and the identified corrections may be sensitive to flow regime and dataset quality.
paper_title: Data-driven identification of multiscale self-similarity and asymptotic matching
